title: Release wave timetable and gate matrix for weekly trains
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a deterministic weekly release wave timetable and an actionable gate matrix that covers feature, canary, RC, and LTS lanes, plus automate RC tagging and release-note extraction.

Background: Our current weekly build process has ad-hoc gating and inconsistent tagging which increases manual overhead for release engineers and delays rollouts. This ticket consolidates cadence rules, defines a matrix for gating (automated checks + manual approvals), and hooks the process into the release-notes automation pipeline.

Deliverables:
- A 'wave timetable' doc that maps weekday -> pipeline stage (build, smoke, canary, RC-tag, freeze, public roll).
- Gate matrix: for each lane (feature, canary, stable, LTS) list required green checks (CI suites, perf baselines, security scan), who can manually approve, and escalation path.
- RC tagging convention and script: deterministic tag name, backfill logic for delayed RCs, and compatibility rules for model/runtime pairing.
- Release-notes automation spec: canonical commit selection, scope mapping (breaking/patch/feature), and changelog synthesis config.
- End-to-end playbook for on-call and release engineers including rollback decision tree and post-release health checks.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Wave timetable published in the Release Train Confluence space with explicit times and responsibilities.
2) Gate matrix implemented as JSON/YAML in the release-config repo and referenced by CI jobs.
3) RC tagging script merged and runs in the build pipeline to create candidate tags automatically when conditions met.
4) Release notes automation produces a draft changelog page for each RC that can be enriched by the release owner.
5) Runbook validated in one dry-run weekly train with no more than 1 manual intervention required.

Notes / Constraints:
- LTS lanes must allow cherry-picks from the stable branch and include a lightweight regression suite that prioritizes critical regressions.
- Autoscaler and Dedicated capacity fluctuations may cause canary failures; gate matrix should include a fallback policy for capacity-induced flakiness.
- Tagging must be stable across private deployments; ensure tag metadata includes model version, quantization profile, and runtime hash.

Next steps (high level):
- Finalize timetable draft and circulate with PM and SRE by 2026-03-02.
- Implement gate matrix schema and a minimal enforcement bot by 2026-03-10.
- Wire RC tagging into the build pipeline and run a dry-run cycle on 2026-03-12.
